issues.reason: Compound concepts requires decomposition atoms for any fused compound unless the idiom bar fires, and that bar's own coherence test takes the literal reading "whenever it is available" — hands being literally shown is exactly what happens here — so the licensed encoding is the nominalization's-of-object oblique, not an opaque undecomposed `show_of_hands` that connects to nothing.

gaps_confirmed: a procedural means-NP ("votes by a show of hands"): Instrument is defined as a tool, substance or conduit and Manner takes only manner adverbs, so nothing decides between Instrument and a preposition-named `(By <event> ...)` oblique for a stated method
new_gaps: the idiom coherence test can never select the lexicalized reading of a semi-transparent conventionalized NP ("a show of hands", "a point of order"), because the literal reading is always "available" for such phrases; a licensed form would need a way to record that the phrase names one conventional procedure while still decomposing it to its parts
defect_summary: The compliant form replaces the fused symbol with the literal nominalization on its own witness — `(Member (sk_show $x) show)` plus its of-argument `(Of (sk_show $x) hand)` — keeping the vote event's link to that show witness; the rest of the whenever-rule stands unchanged.
notes: The reviewer's second gap (no routing for an "N of N" nominal) is not confirmed: the nominalization's-of-object rule and the idiom coherence test together do decide this case.
